item.title: Destin · 2026-11-16 · November 16, 2026 Regular City Council Meeting (City Council): "Welcome to Destin" sign update
item.description: The City's Welcome to Destin sign, located on property controlled by Eglin Air Force Base, sustained significant damage during Hurricane Isaias on October 9, 2026. The sign serves as a prominent gateway feature welcoming residents and visitors to the City of Destin. Following the storm, City staff initiated coordination with Eglin Air Force Base to obtain authorization to access the property, assess the damage, and determine the extent of repairs necessary to restore the sign.

item.title: Destin · 2026-11-16 · November 16, 2026 Regular City Council Meeting (City Council): Update on Indian Trail Property Drainage and Erosion Concerns – Mr. Joe Fitzpatrick
item.description: During the Regular City Council meeting on November 2, 2026, Joe Fitzpatrick requested information about disaster assistance following the hurricane, including assistance the City was pursuing and how residents could report damage. He also described continuing erosion and drainage concerns affecting his Indian Trail property. He said he had obtained a boundary survey and engineering analysis, offered temporary access easements for inspections, and requested a meeting with City officials and staff to develop a cooperative resolution. Councilmember Schmidt made a motion, seconded by Councilmember Stephens, to direct the City Manager to work with [name left out] and appropriate staff on his request and report back to Council in January. The motion passed 6‑0.

item.description: Due to multiple requests for Council consideration of Mobility Fee reductions and waivers, as well as the Council’s prior action to remove the Pine Street extension project from the Mobility Plan, the Council held a Special Meeting on October 13, 2026, to review Mobility Fee rates for potential reductions and to evaluate the projects and priorities identified in the Mobility Plan for possible revisions. At that meeting, Council directed Staff to proceed with amendments to the City's Mobility Fee regulations to address reductions for long-term single-family residential and Community Support Services, allow credit for prior uses regardless of whether a Mobility Fee was previously paid, and to create a Mobility Fee reduction process for the Community Redevelopment Areas (CRAs).

item.title: Destin · 2026-11-16 · November 16, 2026 Regular City Council Meeting (City Council): Replacement of City Truck, 2022 Ford F250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4x4 (Public Works)
item.description: On October 20, 2026, a City-owned 2022 Ford F-250 pickup truck assigned to the Public Works Department was involved in a motor vehicle accident (City employee was not at-fault). The vehicle sustained significant damage and was subsequently determined to be a total loss by the City's insurance provider. The vehicle was utilized to support daily Public Works operations, including roadway maintenance, equipment transportation, and other field activities. Its loss has reduced the Department's available vehicle inventory and created a need for replacement.

item.description: Florida Statute Chapter 166.241 (8) provides that within a fiscal year or within 60 days following the end of the fiscal year a municipality may amend a budget for the year. Section 3.14 of the Charter of the City of Destin provides that at any time during the fiscal year the city manager may transfer all or part of any unencumbered appropriation balance among programs amongst departments. Council may also make such transfers via motion or resolution. The summation of all such transfers by the city council will be included in an ordinance prior to closing of the fiscal year. Our Budget Adoption ordinance also allows for prior year open encumbrances to automatically roll forward to become part of the newly adopted budget. item.title: Destin · 2026-11-02 · November 2, 2026 Regular City Council Meeting (City Council): Hurricane Isaias, Storm Debris Collection Status Update
item.description: On October 9, 2026, Hurricane Isaias impacted the City of Destin, resulting in widespread vegetative debris, downed trees, and damage to public and private property. In response, the City activated its disaster debris removal contract with T.F.R. Enterprises, Inc. (TFR), along with its debris monitoring contract with Volkert, Inc. A pre-collection coordination meeting was held on October 14, 2026, and debris collection operations began shortly thereafter. The City was divided into eleven collection zones to provide an organized and systematic approach to debris removal throughout the community.

item.title: Destin · 2026-11-02 · November 2, 2026 Regular City Council Meeting (City Council): Resolution 26-32 Destin Youth Council Presentation - Mid-Bay Bridge Toll Rates for Local High School Students
item.description: Back in March, 2023 Destin City Council approved a Resolution (23-05) supporting discounted Mid-bay Bridge toll rates for local high school students. To date, no action has been taken by the Mid-bay Bridge authority. On October 22, 2026, the Destin Youth Council voted to once again pursue this endeavor with the Mid-bay Bridge Authority and are seeking support from both Destin City Council and Niceville City Council. Since it has been more than 3 years since Destin City Council adopted the original Resolution (and the Clerk's office is unable to locate a signed copy), the Destin Youth Council is asking Destin City Council to reaffirm its support via adoption of Resolution 26-32. The Destin Youth Council plans to attend the Mid-Bay Bridge Authority meeting on December 10th.

item.description: The Destin City Council created a Youth Council to engage local teens, gather their perspectives on how city policies affect young residents, and offer them opportunities to contribute to the city's decision-making by providing recommendations on youth-related matters. Members of the Destin Youth Council must be high school students who maintain a minimum GPA of 2.25 and reside within the city limits (Destin City Council may appoint up to five non-resident members who attend a local area high school or home school). Students may reapply annually as long as they continue to meet the grade level and eligibility requirements.
